newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Kuehbacher says need strict EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Kuehbacher says need strict EMU criteria.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Thursday the entry criteria for European monetary union had to be interpreted strictly and that a delay in the start of EMU would not help convergence.

Kuehbacher said in the text of a speech that the timetable laid down in the Maastricht Treaty had to be taken seriously, adding that the treaty was formulated in a way which should ensure a stable euro.
Any new timetable would lack credibility, he said.

In the text of a speech due to be delivered in Berlin on Thursday evening, Kuehbacher said the problems that nations were having in meeting the criteria for Maastricht entry presented the risk that those criteria would end up being interpreted "too generously".

"I am quite clearly opposed to any such attempt to start European currency union at any price," he said, adding that only a "clear and strict" interpretation of the criteria would lend the project credibility.

Referring to recent speculation that EMU might have to be delayed from its planned 1999 start-date, Kuehbacher said that unless European Union ministers decided otherwise, "the Maastricht timetable must be taken seriously".
Noting that the Maastricht Treaty had been constructed in such a way that the euro would be a stable currency, he questioned whether there would be any benefits in delaying the EMU start-date.
"...To me it is extremely questionable whether a postponement would lead to any improved (economic) convergence (between nations)," he said.
Moreover, the credibility of a new, politically-determined start-date would "indeed be slight", he added.
